speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I understand your wife is concerned about your recent bizarre and agitated behavior; let's start by asking, have you experienced any hallucinations, such as seeing or hearing things that others do not?

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old male. The patient has been demonstrating bizarre and agitated behavior for the past 6 weeks. He believes that he is being spied on by the NSA which is also controlling his mind. His wife adds that he has been increasingly withdrawn and intermittently depressed over the last 3 months. He was terminated from his job 4 weeks ago after he ceased attending work. Since his unemployment, he has been focused on creating a device to prevent people from controlling his mind.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given the duration of your symptoms, do you have a history of similar episodes or any family history of psychiatric illness? Also, have you been experiencing significant weight loss, sweating, or rapid heartbeat?

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Schizophrenia, paranoid type.

The patient's 6-week history of bizarre behavior, including delusions of persecution (NSA spying/controlling mind) and grandiosity (creating a device to stop mind control), alongside a 3-month prodrome of withdrawal and depression, fulfills the criteria for a psychotic disorder. The specific nature of his delusions and the duration point strongly to schizophrenia.
